cohort: The study involved 21 14- to 15-year-old adolescents prenatally exposed to betamethasone due to threatened preterm birth, and 35 unexposed adolescents as a reference group.
finding: In 14- to 15-year-old adolescents, prenatal glucocorticoid exposure was not associated with differences in IQ scores, ADHD symptoms, metabolic markers, HPAA, or ANS activity, but the betamethasone group exhibited reduced electrocortical activity in the frontal brain region.
birth_weight: Normal weight appropriate for gestational age
gest_age: Median 37+4 gestational weeks (exposed) vs. median 37+6 gestational weeks (unexposed)
